requirements.evidence: Every requirement and contract item is present: `.env.example:1,7-8` sets APP_NAME=PegaFila, APP_LOCALE=pt_BR and keeps APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE=en; `phpunit.xml:22-24` pins all three; `config/mail.php:129-134` sets `mail.markdown.theme` to pegafila and `resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:242-244` puts #0f7490 on the `.button-primary` action button; `lang/pt_BR.json:559,804` adds the two notification subjects; `routes/web.php:16-27` defines `password.request`, `password.email` (throttle:6,1), `password.reset`, `password.update` under `guest`, and `verification.verify` with `auth`+`signed`+`throttle:6,1`; `PasswordResetLinkController.php:26-32` always flashes `passwords.sent`; `NewPasswordController.php:30-56` validates token/email/password, saves it, rotates `remember_token`, fires `PasswordReset` and redirects to `/`; `app/Models/User.php:6,15` implements `MustVerifyEmail`; `VerifyEmailController.php:17-21` fulfils via `EmailVerificationRequest` and redirects to `/`.

conventions.evidence: Mostly follows the project standard: HTTP controllers with server-side validation (`PasswordResetLinkController.php:28`, `NewPasswordController.php:32-36`), the project's Blade/Bulma markup with labels and `{{ }}` escaping (`forgot-password.blade.php:26-43`, `reset-password.blade.php:21-60`), and docs kept in sync (`docs/ops/account-mail.md:1-20`, `CHANGELOG.md:12-13,20`). Deviations: `NewPasswordController.php:32-36` validates three fields inline although conventions reserve inline validation for one or two fields and ask for a Form Request once the rule set grows beyond that; `resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:1-16` and `reset-password.blade.php:1-16` duplicate reusable document scaffolding instead of extracting a Blade component.

security.evidence: No weakness found: all input is validated server-side (`PasswordResetLinkController.php:28`, `NewPasswordController.php:32-36`); the reset write uses `forceFill` with only password/remember_token (`NewPasswordController.php:41-44`), avoiding mass assignment; every view output is escaped with `{{ }}` (`forgot-password.blade.php:32`, `reset-password.blade.php:23,28`); the reset request reveals nothing about account existence (`PasswordResetLinkController.php:30-32`); verification is protected by `auth`, `signed` and `EmailVerificationRequest`'s id/hash check (`routes/web.php:25-27`, `VerifyEmailController.php:17-19`); no secrets or raw HTML are exposed.

tests.evidence: Broad feature coverage: `tests/Feature/PasswordResetTest.php:14-132` covers the form, link sending, unknown address, validation, throttling, token reset, invalid tokens and the password rule set; `tests/Feature/EmailVerificationTest.php:20-65` covers valid, wrong-hash, wrong-id and unsigned links; `tests/Feature/AccountMailTest.php:10-50` covers locale/theme pins, subjects and rendered content. Gaps: `tests/Feature/PasswordResetTest.php:58-63` checks guest-only protection only for `password.request`/`password.email`, not `password.reset`/`password.update`, and `:21-30` asserts only that a `ResetPassword` notification was sent, not the `password.reset` action URL.

simplicity.evidence: The production code is lean and reuses the framework broker and notifications (`PasswordResetLinkController.php:30`, `NewPasswordController.php:38-56`, `VerifyEmailController.php:17-21`), and the theme is the framework default with the brand color changed. There is avoidable duplication: the two auth views repeat the same head/Vite-fallback scaffold (`forgot-password.blade.php:1-16`, `reset-password.blade.php:1-16`) and the verification action-URL assertion appears twice (`AccountMailTest.php:49`, `EmailVerificationTest.php:23-27`).

readability.evidence: Small focused controller methods with clear docblocks (`NewPasswordController.php:16-56`, `PasswordResetLinkController.php:12-33`, `VerifyEmailController.php:11-21`), consistent naming and formatting with the rest of the diff, meaningful test names, and no dead code or leftover debugging output; the views are straightforward and well-labelled (`forgot-password.blade.php:26-43`).

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: environment/phpunit pins, the pegafila theme and config, the two language entries, the reset controllers/routes/views, the verification controller/route, and the tests plus the required docs/changelog updates (`docs/ops/account-mail.md:1-20`, `CHANGELOG.md:12-13,20`). No login, registration, layout, UI translation, SCSS/JS or infrastructure changes were added.

issues.explanation: The reset update validates three fields (token, email, password) with inline `$request->validate`, while the conventions reserve inline validation for one or two fields and call for a Form Request once the rule set grows beyond that.

Both views duplicate the same full document head and Vite/CDN fallback block; extracting that reusable markup into an anonymous Blade component would remove the copy and match the project's component convention.

The guest-only test covers only `password.request` and `password.email`; requirement 4 makes the entire reset flow guests-only, so authenticated access to `password.reset` and `password.update` should be asserted too.

The reset-link test only asserts that `ResetPassword` was sent; it does not assert the notification's action URL points at `password.reset` with the expected token/email, so a broken link route would not be caught (unlike the verification test at `tests/Feature/EmailVerificationTest.php:20-27`).
The verification action-URL assertion duplicates the dedicated assertion in `tests/Feature/EmailVerificationTest.php:20-27`; keeping it in one place would avoid the repeated coverage.

review.summary: This change adds the pt-BR account e-mails: env/phpunit locale pins, the pegafila markdown theme, the missing notification subject translations, guest-only password-reset controllers/routes/views, and the signed e-mail verification route, with extensive feature tests and docs. All requirements and the security model are covered; the score is 4 rather than 5 because of a duplicated view scaffold, a three-field inline validation that the conventions assign to a Form Request, and a few test gaps around guest-only reset routes and the reset notification URL.
